teaser.text: Emerson Electric sells the hardware and software that keep industrial processes moving, measured and under control. Its business becomes clearer when we follow one dollar from a plant’s need, through Emerson’s products and customers, to the maintenance and upgrades that bring the customer back.

stock.title: Emerson stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Emerson’s stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios against software growth, project conversion, cash generation and valuation.
stock.opening: Emerson’s weighted value reaches $162.12 in October 2027 and $192.55 in October 2029. It hinges on software growth, project conversion and cash generation sufficient to manage debt.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Emerson’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Emerson’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast assigns 28% probability to the bear case, 54% to the base case and 18% to the bull case. The base case reaches $170.37 in October 2027 and $199.63 in October 2029. By October 2029, the bear case reaches $99.30 and the bull case $316.37.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Emerson?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives earnings of 3,500, 3,550 and 3,700 as weak project conversion and late renewals keep growth near 1–2%. The bull case reaches 5,700 by 2029 because ACV growth, orders, backlog conversion and AspenTech cross-selling all strengthen. ACV was 1.68 billion, up 9%, and June-quarter orders grew 7%. Emerson’s 6.55 adjusted-EPS guide and 8.00 target for 2028 support growth, but they are targets rather than net-income guarantees. The forecast excludes the 82 million tariff refund, disposal gains and acquisition accounting charges.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Emerson really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was $3,676 million in fiscal 2025. Capital spending was $431 million, leaving free cash flow of $3,245 million. Free cash flow reached 18.0% of revenue, compared with 12.7% in 2022. That is stronger evidence than adjusted earnings alone because it shows money left after operating payments and investment in assets.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Emerson?

paragraphs.text: Free-cash-flow yield is 3.6%, compared with a stated real free-cash-flow yield of 3.3%. Free cash flow can repay debt, fund acquisitions, or support dividends and buybacks; the 1.4% dividend yield measures only what shareholders receive directly. “Real” free cash flow has no clear meaning here until its adjustment is defined.

dividend.title: Emerson dividend
dividend.meta_description: Emerson's dividend rises in the forecast, while free cash flow shows how the cash is allocated.
dividend.opening: Emerson's forecast dividend rises from 2.33 to 2.57 per share, from a latest 0.555 quarterly rate. Free cash flow was $3.245 billion in fiscal 2025, and across five years shareholder payments absorbed about $10.6 billion of roughly $12.3 billion in free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo examines Emerson's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Emerson pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise steadily in the base case from 2.33 to 2.45 and then 2.57 per share. The bear case pauses at 2.22 before reaching 2.29, while the bull case reaches 2.77. The base reflects the latest 0.555 quarterly rate, the five-year record of increases and planned dividend payments of about 1.2 billion; debt and competing cash needs make repeated bull-case increases less likely.

blocks.heading: Is Emerson's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left after operations pay for necessary capital spending. Emerson generated $3.676 billion of operating cash in fiscal 2025. After $431 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $3.245 billion.

Dividends made a steady claim on that pool, while buybacks varied sharply. Across five years, shareholder payments absorbed about $10.6 billion of roughly $12.3 billion in free cash flow. In fiscal 2023, buybacks helped push total shareholder payments above that year’s free cash flow, because disposal proceeds supplied additional cash.

blocks.heading: What is Emerson's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: Emerson Electric is an industrial automation company whose equipment, control systems and software help factories and process plants operate. At $162.15 a share on October 16, 2026, the market is paying for a larger business that must produce much more profit and cash.

Free-cash-flow yield is 3.6%, compared with a stated real free-cash-flow yield of 3.3%. Free cash flow can repay debt, fund acquisitions, or support dividends and buybacks; the 1.4% dividend yield measures only what shareholders receive directly. “Real” free cash flow has no clear meaning here until its adjustment is defined.

earnings.title: Emerson earnings: next results and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Emerson reports next on November 4, 2026; watch whether software revenue rebounds with ACV and cash supports lower net debt.
earnings.opening: Emerson's next results are expected on November 4, 2026. Watch whether software revenue rebounds while ACV continues to grow.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Emerson's business works, how it compares with rivals, who manages it and what risks it carries.

blocks.heading: What has Emerson guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Emerson’s fiscal year ends in September. Its August guidance raised underlying sales growth from 3% to 3.5% and moved adjusted earnings per share to the top of its previous range. Underlying growth strips out currency translation and major acquisitions or disposals, so it shows more clearly what the existing business sold.

For the year to September 2026, management promises 3.5% underlying sales growth, $6.55 adjusted EPS and $3,600 million of free cash flow. It also guides to $1,000 million of share repurchases and $1,200 million of dividends.

blocks.heading: Has Emerson kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast adjusted earnings per share in a US$5.85–US$6.05 range. It forecast free cash flow in a US$3.2–US$3.3 billion range. Actual results were US$6.00 and US$3.245 billion, so both operating promises landed inside their ranges. The buyback promise was weaker: the plan called for approximately US$2 billion, while actual repurchases were US$1,167 million.

blocks.heading: What do Emerson's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Sales rose from $4,553 million to $4,873 million. Operating income rose from $829 million to $1,001 million. Matching-quarter comparisons matter because project shipments and software renewals can make adjacent quarters misleading.

Underlying profitability still improved. Adjusted EPS rose from $1.52 to $1.71. Adjusted EBITA margin rose from 26.0% to 26.7%, despite restructuring, acquisition-related costs and discrete taxes. Operating cash flow reached $1,425 million. Free cash flow reached $1,323 million, though the refund contributed to the improvement.
